claim.pdf_says: In both `ALTERNATE RECORD KEY IS` and `RECORD KEY IS`, only ALTERNATE and RECORD carry an underline; KEY and IS are NOT underlined (verified at 300 dpi on the printed glyphs).
claim.markdown_says: The figure note (ISO_COBOL.md line 14770) lists `RECORD KEY` among the underlined words - "...`ORGANIZATION`, `INDEXED`, `RECORD KEY`, `RESERVE`, `SHARING`..." - and then in the very next sentence lists `KEY` among the words that are NOT underlined: "`IS`, `TO`, `MODE`, `KEY`, `WITH`, `WHEN`, `FILE`, `AREA`, `AREAS`, and `OTHER` are not underlined."
claim.why_it_matters: The figure note contradicts itself about a word whose underlining decides whether it is a required word or an optional word. A reader taking the first list at face value would treat KEY as required and reject the legal `RECORD IS data-name-5` / `ALTERNATE RECORD IS data-name-2` spellings - the falsely-restrictive direction.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed on both sides. PDF: rendered page 342 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v342/spec_p342.png) and cropped the two clause headers at 3x magnification. In `ALTERNATE RECORD KEY IS` (12.4.5.1 Format 1 (indexed)) there are exactly TWO separate horizontal rules with a clear gap between them - one spanning A-L-T-E-R-N-A-T-E, one spanning R-E-C-O-R-D - and the baseline under KEY and under IS is bare. In the standalone `RECORD KEY IS` clause lower on the page there is exactly ONE rule, spanning R-E-C-O-R-D only; KEY and IS carry no rule. So the PDF unambiguously prints KEY as a non-underlined (optional) word in both places. Markdown: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 14770 is quoted accurately by the claim - the underlined-words list ends '...`ORGANIZATION`, `INDEXED`, `RECORD KEY`, `RESERVE`, `SHARING`, `ALL`, `NO`, `READ`, `ONLY`.' and the immediately following sentence reads '`IS`, `TO`, `MODE`, `KEY`, `WITH`, `WHEN`, `FILE`, `AREA`, `AREAS`, and `OTHER` are not underlined.' Both quotes are verbatim. Refutation attempts that failed: (1) not reflow/wrapping/page-break furniture - the defect is a token inside a single prose line, not a layout artifact; (2) not a misquote - both sources match the claim word for word; (3) the 'disambiguation' reading (that `RECORD KEY` names WHICH occurrence of RECORD is meant, since RECORD already appears twice earlier in the list) does not hold, because the note establishes its own disambiguation convention in the very same paragraph - '`FILE` in `FILE STATUS` is not underlined; `STATUS` is' - and the bare two-word entry does not use it; as written, inside a list captioned 'Underlined in the printed standard', a two-word backticked entry asserts both words are underlined; (4) it does change meaning - underlining is the standard's required-word notation, and the code fence carries no underline information at all, so this note is the ONLY carrier of required-vs-optional for this figure. Scope check: grepped every figure note in ISO_COBOL.md for the `RECORD KEY` entry - line 14770 is the sole occurrence, so this is an isolated defect, not a pattern. Verified as a side-check that the note is otherwise faithful: ORGANIZATION is underlined and the trailing IS is not, exactly as the note states.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, but slightly over-stated in impact. The defect: in the page-342 figure note (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 14770), the list of words underlined in the printed standard contains the two-word entry `RECORD KEY`. The printed page shows the underline running under RECORD only - two separate rules (ALTERNATE, RECORD) in `ALTERNATE RECORD KEY IS`, one rule (RECORD) in the standalone `RECORD KEY IS` - with KEY and IS bare in both places. The entry should read `RECORD`, or simply be dropped since `RECORD` already appears twice in the same list; the following sentence's placement of `KEY` in the not-underlined list is correct and matches the PDF. Impact is bounded because the contradiction is self-flagging: the two lists disagree one sentence apart, so a careful reader is warned rather than silently misled - 'cosmetic' severity is defensible, though 'minor' is arguably the better label since the note is the only place underlining (required vs optional word) survives transcription. Fix is a one-token edit to line 14770.
